title: Local properties of a smooth relative curve over a trait
statement:
Let $R$ be a discrete valuation ring with uniformizer $\pi$, residue field $k=R/(\pi)$ and fraction field $K$ [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring]. Let $f:X\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ be a smooth morphism whose every nonempty fibre is of pure dimension one [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-pure-dimension]. Then $f$ is flat and locally of finite presentation, and $X$ is locally Noetherian [def-weil-flat-morphism, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation, pqf-def-locnoeth]. Every local ring of $X$ is regular and an integrally closed domain [def-weil-regular-scheme, def-weil-pbc-normal-ring]. Every local ring has dimension at most two; at every closed point of the special fibre $X_k$ its dimension is exactly two [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring, def-pc-scheme-fibre]. More precisely for $x$ over $s\in\operatorname{Spec}R$,
$$\dim\mathcal O_{X,x}=\dim R_s+\dim\mathcal O_{X_s,x},\qquad \dim\mathcal O_{X_s,x}\le1,$$
and the latter dimension equals one at a closed point of either nonempty fibre. Empty schemes and empty fibres are permitted. No quasi-compactness, separatedness, excellence or residue-field perfection is assumed.

source.place: Agent scheme-local assembly of inherited step 7; Tags 07NF (lemma-regular-goes-up), 00ON (lemma-dimension-base-fibre-equals-total), 0AFS (lemma-localization-of-regular-local-is-regular); morphisms.tex Tag 01V4 (definition-smooth) for the smooth affine-local convention.

proof.text: Every ideal of $R$ is principal, hence finitely generated, so $R$ is Noetherian. By [lem-sc-dvr-dimension-one], $\dim R=1$. Its maximal ideal is $(\pi)$, so the definition of regular local ring makes $R$ regular local. By [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-localization], $R$ is a regular ring. Its primes are exactly $(0)$ and $(\pi)$: a nonzero prime strictly below the maximal ideal would give a chain of length two. Thus every nonempty open of $\operatorname{Spec}R$ is either the whole spectrum or its generic point $\operatorname{Spec}K$; an open containing the closed point contains a basic open $D(a)$ with $a$ a unit. The coordinate rings of these two opens are regular: $R$ as above and the field $K$ by the dimension-zero definition.

By [lem-pc-smooth-flat], $f$ is flat and locally of finite presentation. Use the affine-local smooth-ring-map convention explicitly included in [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]: around every $x$ choose $U=\operatorname{Spec}B$ mapping into an affine open $V=\operatorname{Spec}A$ of the base with $A\to B$ smooth. Step 1 makes $A$ regular, so [lem-weil-pbc-regular-ring-smooth-ascent] makes $B$ regular, in particular Noetherian. These $U$ cover $X$, proving local Noetherianity and regularity by [def-weil-regular-scheme] and [pqf-def-locnoeth]. This also supplies finite-presentation affine charts whenever they are used below.

source.place: Tag 07NF, lemma-regular-goes-up; morphisms.tex Tags 01V5, definition-smooth, and 02H6, lemma-smooth-formally-smooth

proof.text: For a point $x$ in one of these $U$, let $\mathfrak q$ be its prime of $B$. The affine-stalk isomorphism [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-stalk-localization] identifies $\mathcal O_{X,x}$ with $B_{\mathfrak q}$. This is regular local by regularity of $B$. By [lem-weil-pbc-regular-ring-normal], $B$ is normal, which means precisely that each $B_{\mathfrak q}$ is an integrally closed domain [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring]. This proves both stalk assertions without claiming that a disconnected $X$ is integral.

Fix $x$ over $s$, and write $A=R_s$, $T=\mathcal O_{X,x}$. Both are Noetherian local rings by Steps 1--3. The map $A\to T$ is local and flat by [def-weil-flat-morphism]. Apply the local-ring form of [lem-weil-pbc-flat-height-formula] at their maximal ideals: since localization of a local ring at its maximal ideal is itself, it gives $\dim T=\dim A+\dim(T/\mathfrak m_AT)$. By [lem-sbc-scheme-fibre-stalk-quotient], the last quotient is canonically $\mathcal O_{X_s,x}$. This proves the claimed equality for every point, not just closed points.

Each fibre is locally of finite type over $\kappa(s)$. Indeed, in a finite-presentation chart $A_0\to B=A_0[t_1,\ldots,t_n]/(g_1,\ldots,g_m)$ from Step 2, the fibre chart is $\operatorname{Spec}C$ with $C=B\otimes_{A_0}\kappa(s)=\kappa(s)[t_1,\ldots,t_n]/(\bar g_1,\ldots,\bar g_m)$ by [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra]. Here $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ factors through the open $V=\operatorname{Spec}A_0$ containing $s$, and by [lem-weil-pbc-open-preimage-fibre-product] (applied to the first projection $X_s\to X$ and the open $U=\operatorname{Spec}B$, and to $U\to V$) together with the pasting of fibre-product squares, the preimage of $U$ in $X_s=X\times_{\operatorname{Spec}R}\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)$ [def-pc-scheme-fibre] is the open subscheme $U\times_V\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)\cong\operatorname{Spec}C$. As the $U$ cover $X$, these affine opens cover the fibre. Since this nonempty fibre is pure of dimension one by hypothesis, apply [lem-sbc-equidimensional-open-local-dimension] with $Y=X_s$, $O=Y$, $n=1$: its local topological dimension is one at every point. On a fibre chart containing $x$, [lem-weil-pbc-dimension-at-point-local-ring-trdeg] and [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-stalk-localization] give $1=\dim\mathcal O_{X_s,x}+\operatorname{trdeg}_{\kappa(s)}\kappa(x)$. Nonnegativity of transcendence degree therefore gives $\dim\mathcal O_{X_s,x}\le1$. Local topological dimension is unchanged by taking an open neighbourhood, directly from its neighbourhood definition.

source.place: Varieties Tag 0A21, lemma-dimension-locally-algebraic, (5),(10); Algebra Tag 00P1, lemma-dimension-at-a-point-finite-type-field; Schemes Tags 01I4, lemma-fibre-product-affine-schemes, and 01JQ, lemma-fibre-product-affines

proof.text: If $x$ is closed in $X_s$, it is closed in each affine fibre chart containing it, so its prime in that finite-type $\kappa(s)$-algebra is maximal. By [lem-weil-pbc-closed-point-dimension-local-ring], the local-ring dimension equals the local topological dimension, already one in Step 5. Step 1 gives $\dim R_s=0$ at the generic point (a field) and $\dim R_s=1$ at the closed point. Combining these values with Steps 4--5 bounds every $\dim\mathcal O_{X,x}$ by two. At a closed point of the special fibre, Step 4 gives exactly $1+1=2$. At a closed point of the generic fibre, its fibre local-ring dimension is one, as asserted.

All arguments are on neighbourhoods of a specified point. If $X$ or a fibre is empty, it has no such points and the corresponding universal assertions are vacuous. Neither affine charts nor any ring lemma above assumes global quasi-compactness, separatedness, excellence, or perfection of the residue field.
